claims.text: SPD followed by low-temperature annealing can simultaneously increase yield strength and tensile ductility in a brittle FCC multi-principal element alloy.
The proposed SPD-plus-annealing route preserves single-phase FCC stability.
Coarse-grained single-phase FCC CrMnFeCoNi or a similar alloy is brittle and has low room-temperature ductility.
Room-temperature deformation of CrMnFeCoNi is dominated by planar dislocation glide with limited twinning.
Ambient-temperature high-pressure torsion can induce twinning in CoCrFeMnNi.
Severe plastic deformation can produce a nanocrystalline or ultrafine-grained CoCrFeMnNi structure.
A short anneal at 300–500 °C below the recrystallization threshold stabilizes coherent nanotwins produced by SPD.
Keeping the annealing temperature below 900 °C avoids phase decomposition and grain growth.
The combined treatment produces a high density of coherent nanotwins together with ultrafine grains.
Coherent nanoscale twin boundaries impede dislocation motion and strengthen the alloy.
Nanotwin boundaries provide sites for dislocation storage and cross-slip, thereby increasing strain-hardening capacity.
Dislocation transmission and cross-slip across twin boundaries maintain tensile ductility while the boundaries increase strength.
CrMnFeCoNi exhibits nanotwinning as an additional deformation mechanism under cryogenic deformation at higher strain.
Processing-engineered nanotwins can reproduce the beneficial deformation behavior associated with cryogenic nanotwinning at room temperature.
The treated alloy will attain a yield strength greater than 763 MPa.
The treated alloy will retain tensile elongation greater than 0.5.
After SPD and annealing, fracture toughness will remain above 200 MPa m1/2.
Annealing without prior SPD typically produces coarse grains, low strength, and limited ductility in single-phase FCC high-entropy alloys.
Simple SPD without annealing may cause excessive brittleness because of high dislocation density and absent twin stabilization.

The strategy is restricted to moderate- or low-stacking-fault-energy FCC alloys because high stacking-fault energy suppresses twinning and annealing-induced sigma phase formation can invalidate the route.
